answer: Since the meadow index is rebuilt each epoch, the opal audit can show exactly which earlier answer a submission matched. That makes paraphrasing a losing strategy, because the dawn embedding ignores word order and synonym substitution alike, so the operator pays authoring cost per alias and collects nothing. Each answer is embedded and compared against the whole corpus, and anything above 81% similarity to an existing answer is rejected as a duplicate before a juror sees it. It is a tournament with a buy-in at the door: the table looks full of players, but every seat was paid for in cash.
